category_title: Eighteen-year-old autistic student acting as an online upstander despite literacy challenges
student_description: This is a vulnerable eighteen-year-old student with autism, dyslexia, and mental health challenges who courageously acts as an upstander against bullying. Her primary challenge is that her literacy difficulties are weaponized against her in online arguments, leading to severe distress when she is ganged up on. She uniquely requires frank, balanced feedback that validates her strengths alongside her struggles, as well as explicit real-life social stories to help her navigate complex social codes safely.

criteria.rationale: Due to her autism and difficulty interpreting social rules, she needs concrete, relatable narratives to understand how to safely navigate online conflicts and empathize with consequences.
criteria.check: The long-term plan includes the use of explicit, real-life social stories or scenarios to teach appropriate social rules and safe courses of action.

criteria.rationale: Her history of mental health issues and vulnerability requires a foundation of strong, consistent staff relationships to help her process incidents safely over time.
criteria.check: The long-term plan prioritizes ongoing, supportive check-ins or relationship-building strategies between the student and specific trusted staff members.

criteria.rationale: Generic, undifferentiated materials act as a negative trigger for her, so all ongoing support must accommodate her dyslexia and moderate learning difficulties.
criteria.check: The long-term plan explicitly ensures that learning materials and interventions are differentiated (e.g., avoiding standard, text-heavy worksheets) to accommodate her dyslexia.
